questions.stem: After antibiotic treatment, resistant bacteria become common. The most accurate explanation is that the antibiotic:
options: Selected resistant variants already present in the population
Taught every bacterium how to resist
Prevented all bacterial reproduction
Converted viruses into bacteria
questions.explanation: Resistance variants arise before exposure through mutation or gene transfer. Antibiotic treatment removes susceptible competitors and increases the relative success of resistant cells.

questions.stem: The same underlying forelimb bone pattern in whales, bats and humans is strongest evidence for:

Common ancestry followed by divergent evolution
Inheritance of acquired characters

questions.explanation: Homologous structures share an underlying developmental origin despite different functions, supporting descent from a common ancestor and later divergence.

questions.stem: A large randomly mating population has no mutation, migration or selection. Which outcome is expected across generations?

All individuals become heterozygous

questions.explanation: These conditions approximate Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, under which allele and genotype frequencies remain stable apart from sampling error.

questions.stem: A few individuals colonise an isolated island and carry allele frequencies unlike the source population. This is an example of:
options: Artificial selection
Convergent evolution
Gene flow into a large population

questions.explanation: A new population founded by a small sample may begin with unrepresentative allele frequencies, a form of genetic drift called the founder effect.

questions.stem: A population contains 30 AA, 50 Aa and 20 aa individuals. What is the frequency of allele A?
questions.explanation: There are 200 alleles at this locus. A alleles total 2×30 + 50 = 110, so their frequency is 110/200 = 0.55.

questions.explanation: Chance differences in which individuals reproduce can change allele frequencies, especially in small populations. This is genetic drift rather than a directed response to need.

questions.stem: In the same environment, which genotype has the highest measured reproductive contribution in this sample?
options: P, because it has the most adults
The data show only mutation rates

questions.explanation: Relative contribution per adult is 2 for P, 3 for Q and 1 for R. Q is highest by this measure; body size or adult abundance alone would not establish it.
